messages.subject: 2 action buttons 1 table
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I have some problem with the reactivity of shiny.

I have a (global) data frame called table.of.peaks which the app displays trough peakTable() function. When the 'Add' button is pressed, the app adds a new row to the table (the data of the row is collected from the UI input fields "separated" by using isolate() function). 

The sequence of function calling is the following (starting from the function where the input$add.button takes place):
  1. readPeak() - the data from the UI is collected and sent (as a one row data frame, let's call it Row) to the function from where the readPeak() have been called (makeTable())
  2. makeTable() - the Row here is added to the global table.of.peaks table, and the function return with this global data frame
  3. peakTable() - the global table.of.peaks variable (return value of makeTable() function) is displayed
During operation, always the actual value of the table can be seen, and when the Add button is pressed, the table is updated and printed out again.

My question is, can i add a Delete button to the app that works the same way as the Add button (get the row index we want to delete from the UI) without using Javascript or other "external" solutions? The app would work the same, but table would be updated from a func. called for example delPeak() if the Delete button is pressed. So the sequence would look like delPeak() -> makeTable() -> peakTable(), and if Add button is pressed the sequence would be the same as above.

I didn't include any source code, because there aren't any errors yet, i'm just planning the implementation, and searching for a simple method.

Thanks for the help in advance.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: 2 action buttons 1 table
parts: You should probably use a reactive value (see ?reactiveValues) to store the table; and have two observers, one of which reads input$add.button (btw you should avoid putting periods in input/output IDs) and adds to the table reactive value, and the other of which reads the delete button and removes from the table reactive value.
